data.question_title: The number of reflexive relations of a set with four elements is equal to
data.explanation_txt:
Consider a set \(A = \{a_1, a_2, a_3, ... , a_n \} \)

\( A \times A = \{ (a_1,a_1), (a_a, a_2), ... , (a_2,a_2), ... (a_3, a_3), ..., (a_n, a_n) \} \)

The reflexive relations are subsets of \( \{ (a_1,a_1), (a_2,a_2), ... (a_n,a_n) \} \).

So, the superset of reflexive relations has \(n\) elements.

Total number of reflexive relations in a set with n elements \(=2^{n} \).

Therefore, total number of reflexive relation set with 4 elements \(=2^{4} \).

data.question_title: \(x^{x} \) has a stationary point at :
data.explanation_txt:
Let \(y=x^{x} \)\( \Rightarrow \)

\(\log y=x.\log x,\; \; \; \; (x>0)\)

Differentiating \(\cfrac{dy}{dx} =x^{x} (1+\log x)\);

\({\mkern1mu\raise1pt\hbox{.}\mkern1mu\raise4pt\hbox{.}\mkern1mu\raise1pt\hbox{.}\mkern1mu} \cfrac{dy}{dx} =0\)

\[ \Rightarrow \log x=-1 \Rightarrow x=e^{-1} =\cfrac{1}{e} \]

\({\mkern1mu\raise1pt\hbox{.}\mkern1mu\raise4pt\hbox{.}\mkern1mu\raise1pt\hbox{.}\mkern1mu} \) Stationary point is \(x=\cfrac{1}{e} \)

\[\cfrac{d^{2} y}{dx^{2} } =x^{x} (1+\log x)^{2} +x^{x} .\cfrac{1}{x} \]

When \(x=\cfrac{1}{e} ,\; \; \cfrac{d^{2} y}{dx^{2} } =\left(\cfrac{1}{e} \right)^{(1/e)-1} >0\)

Therefore \(\textit{y}\) is minimum at \(x=\cfrac{1}{e} \) and minimum value \(=\left(\cfrac{1}{e} \right)^{1/e} =e^{-1/e} \).

data.question_title: The rules of etiquette in American restaurants depend upon a number of factors: the physical location of the restaurant, e.g. rural or urban, the type of restaurant, e.g. Informal or formal, and certain standards that are more universal. In other words, some standards of etiquette vary significantly while other standard apply almost anywhere. Learning the proper etiquette in a particular type of restaurant or in a particular area may sometimes require instruction, but more commonly it simply requires sensitivity and experience. For example, while it is acceptable to read a magazine in a coffee shop, it is inappropriate to do the same in a more luxurious setting. And, if you are eating in a more rustic setting it may be fine to tuck your napkin into your shirt, but if you were in a sophisticated urban restaurant this behavior would demonstrate a lack of manners. It is safe to say, however, that in virtually every restaurant it is unacceptable to discriminatory throw your food on the floor. The conclusion we can most likely draw from the above is that while the types and locations of the restaurant determines etiquette appropriate to them, some rules apply to all restaurants.
